newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus oil refinery restructured but state owned.
newsitem.headline: Belarus oil refinery restructured but state owned.

text.p: Belarus, fresh from signing a union treaty with Russia, has restructured its Novopolotsk oil refinery into a state-owned joint-stock corporation, a State Property Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
Under a ministry decree, the refinery, also known as Naftan, has a charter capital of 1.5 trillion Belarussian roubles.
Novopolotsk has an annual capacity of 510,000 barrels per day (bpd), and is coveted by Russian oil producers for its location in the northeastern part of Belarus near the Baltics.

The spokesman said any sale of the facility's shares would take place by presidential decree, adding that Russian oil companies LUKoil and YUKOS had expressed interest in acquiring stakes. The two companies supply the refinery with crude oil, but the facility is working far below capacity.
Minsk said last month that it wanted an investor ready to pump $350 million into the refinery.
Novopolotsk had drafted a plan in December 1996 to give the two Russian oil producers a controlling stake, but Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko vetoed it.
Russia and Belarus signed a Union Treaty on Wednesday calling for broad economic cooperation measures.
Belarus's second oil refinery, Mozyr, with an annual capacity of 320,000 bpd, is in the southern central part of the former Soviet republic.
